guidance.title: Speech sound and phonology

portal.label: ASHA Practice Portal · Speech Sound Disorders

evidence_map.label: ASHA Evidence Map · Speech Sound Disorders

guidance.summary: For idiopathic childhood speech sound concerns, consider speech patterns, intelligibility, hearing, and linguistic background alongside test performance.

components.label: History and language background
components.description: Gather family concerns, languages and dialects, hearing history, and reports of classroom participation.

components.label: Hearing and oral structures
components.description: Check available hearing information and examine speech structures and movement when relevant.

components.label: Words and connected speech
components.description: Compare structured productions with conversation or retelling; analyze sound contexts, patterns, and consistency.

components.label: Intelligibility in everyday settings
components.description: Consider how well familiar and unfamiliar listeners understand the child across communication settings.

components.label: Stimulability
components.description: Consider imitation of difficult sounds to clarify the production profile and possible intervention targets.

notes: This Portal page focuses on idiopathic disorders in preschool and school-age children. Motor, structural, and sensory causes require condition-specific guidance.
These considerations supplement clinical judgment; the site does not prescribe a complete evaluation.

guidance.title: Spoken language, vocabulary, and narrative

portal.label: ASHA Practice Portal · Spoken Language Disorders

evidence_map.label: ASHA Evidence Map · Spoken Language Disorders

guidance.summary: Consider the child's communication across language domains and contexts; a vocabulary measure samples one part of this broader profile.

components.label: History and everyday concerns
components.description: Gather developmental, language and dialect, caregiver, teacher, and hearing information.

components.label: Language beyond isolated words
components.description: Consider comprehension and expression across semantics, grammar, conversation, narrative, and expository discourse.

components.label: Formal and informal evidence
components.description: Choose measures that fit the communication profile and language background; include context-sensitive observations.

components.label: Learning potential
components.description: Dynamic assessment can examine response to teaching alongside other assessment findings.

components.label: Literacy connections
components.description: Consider developmentally relevant reading, writing, or preliteracy information within a broader language evaluation.

notes: Translated tests and tests used outside their intended populations do not support reporting their standard scores.
This page addresses developmental spoken-language disorders; acquired adult aphasia has separate guidance.

studies.title: The Classification Accuracy of a Dynamic Assessment of Inferential Word Learning for Bilingual English/Spanish-Speaking School-Age Children
studies.method: English-only test–teach–test word-learning protocol; linear discriminant analysis combined posttest scores and examiner modifiability ratings.
studies.population: Spanish/English bilingual children ages 5:9–9:7, recruited from three U.S. elementary schools.
studies.sample_size: 31 children: 10 with language disorder and 21 with typical language.
studies.cutoff: No interpretable single cutoff for the combined discriminant model (Table 3, footnote a).
studies.findings: The combined model yielded 90% sensitivity and 90.5% specificity in this sample (Table 3).
studies.limitation: Small development sample; the authors call for replication and cross-validation. The dynamic task was administered in English only to bilingual children. This research protocol did not validate PPVT-5, and its accuracy should not be transferred to commercial vocabulary tests or other populations.
studies.locator: Petersen et al. (2020), Abstract, Methods, Table 3 and Dynamic Assessment Results; personally rechecked

guidance.title: Stuttering, cluttering, and fluency

portal.label: ASHA Practice Portal · Stuttering / Cluttering / Fluency

evidence_map.label: ASHA Evidence Map · Stuttering / Cluttering / Fluency

guidance.summary: Visible disfluency frequency alone may miss the person's experience. Consider overt speech features, avoidance, reactions, and participation.

components.label: History and variability
components.description: Consider onset, course, prior treatment, and situations where speech concerns vary.

components.label: Speech across tasks and settings
components.description: Consider conversation, narrative, and speech outside the clinic, including rate, disfluency characteristics, and associated behaviors.

components.label: The speaker's experience
components.description: Consider effort, coping, negative reactions, avoidance, and the person's own report.

components.label: Participation and partner perspectives
components.description: Gather family or educator perspectives and examine educational, social, or vocational impact.

notes: Age-specific considerations differ for preschool children, school-age children, adolescents, and adults.
Little observable stuttering does not necessarily mean little impact.

guidance.title: Adult aphasia and functional communication
guidance.summary: For acquired adult aphasia, combine language findings with access needs, communication in daily life, and the person's priorities.

components.label: History and language use
components.description: Consider onset, medical context, premorbid language use, and languages needed for everyday activities.

components.label: Language across modalities
components.description: Consider spoken comprehension and expression together with reading and writing.

components.label: Response and access demands
components.description: Consider motor speech, cognition, hearing, vision, pointing or writing ability, and fatigue.

components.label: Activity and participation
components.description: Consider everyday communication, interpersonal interactions, and environmental supports or barriers.

notes: The Portal page's scope is acquired aphasia in adults; primary progressive aphasia needs additional condition-specific sources.
Document assessment modifications and their implications for interpreting standardized scores.

guidance.title: Cognitive communication: executive function

portal.label: ASHA Practice Portal · Executive Function Deficits

evidence_map.label: ASHA Evidence Map · Executive Function Deficits

guidance.summary: Executive-function guidance applies across the lifespan. Connect test findings to real tasks and to the person's baseline and context.

components.label: Baseline and reported changes
components.description: Use patient and partner interviews to understand concerns and changes from usual functioning.

components.label: Cognitive and language demands
components.description: Consider interacting skills and whether language difficulty affects performance; nonverbal measures may help.

components.label: Everyday task performance
components.description: Consider assessment in relevant settings, where attention and planning demands may differ from quiet testing.

components.label: Team evidence and reassessment
components.description: Review other professionals' findings, avoid unnecessary duplicate testing, and consider fatigue and practice effects.

notes: This guidance concerns executive function, not every cause of cognitive change.
Standardized results may not capture difficulties under everyday time pressure or distraction.

guidance.title: Adult brain injury: cognitive communication

portal.label: ASHA Practice Portal · Traumatic Brain Injury (Adults)

evidence_map.label: ASHA Evidence Map · Traumatic Brain Injury (Adults)

guidance.summary: For adults with traumatic brain injury, connect speech-language and cognitive findings with daily roles, medical context, and team assessment.

components.label: Injury and recovery context
components.description: Consider medical history, alertness, sensory and motor status, medications, and personal communication priorities.

components.label: Fit of the measure
components.description: Check whether tasks and norms fit the individual's injury, impairment, and language background.

components.label: Function in daily activities
components.description: Compare structured scores with communication and task performance in everyday settings.

components.label: Supports and barriers
components.description: Consider environmental barriers, communication partners, cognitive aids, and relevant follow-up services.

notes: This source concerns adult TBI. Pediatric injury and other etiologies require their own guidance.
SLPs assess communication and related function; this site does not diagnose TBI.

guidance.title: Functional communication and AAC

portal.label: ASHA Practice Portal · Augmentative and Alternative Communication

evidence_map.label: ASHA Evidence Map · Augmentative and Alternative Communication

guidance.summary: When AAC is relevant, consider communication needs, existing modalities, access, partners, and environments across the lifespan.

components.label: Communication needs and priorities
components.description: Consider what the person needs to communicate and whether support supplements speech or provides another means.

components.label: Current communication and partner input
components.description: Gather observations and caregiver or partner reports of communication beyond the assessment session.

components.label: Access and feature fit
components.description: Consider symbols, vocabulary, selection methods, positioning, portability, and user preferences.

components.label: Trials and everyday use
components.description: Consider dynamic assessment, trials, family support, and barriers in the environments where communication occurs.

notes: AAC assessment is an ongoing process; an initial device trial may not resolve all questions.
This AAC source does not cover every form of functional-communication assessment.
ASHA links provide context; ASHA has not endorsed this site's catalog or shortlist.
